topic: CrowdStrike global IT outage on July 19, 2024

fact_checks.description: The outage is anchored to July 19, 2024
matching_facts: On July 19, 2024, a global IT outage was triggered by a faulty update from CrowdStrike, a leading cybersecurity firm.
July 19, 2024, 05:27 UTC: CrowdStrike identified the issue and reverted the changes, but by then, many systems had already been affected.

fact_checks.description: CrowdStrike Falcon is identified as the affected product
matching_facts: On July 19, 2024, a flawed update to CrowdStrike’s Falcon sensor, a cybersecurity tool widely used to protect devices like computer workstations and servers, resulted in a global IT outage.

fact_checks.description: Windows systems are identified as affected
matching_facts:
The

widespread outage that occurred on Friday 19 July as a result of a CrowdStrike configuration push that put Windows machines into a boot loop may well have been the largest digital systems availability incident that the world has ever seen.
Outages were experienced worldwide, reflecting the wide use of Microsoft Windows and CrowdStrike software by global corporations in numerous business sectors.
The global outage of specific Microsoft-enabled systems and servers was isolated to a faulty software update released by CrowdStrike

Crowdstrike Update - July 23rd
Earlier today, Crowdstrike released an update to the EDR agent to aid in the resolution of the ongoing issues impacting Windows OS-based systems.
The update affected Windows systems, leading to widespread disruptions across multiple sectors, including airlines, healthcare, banking, and public services.

fact_checks.description: A faulty content/software update is identified as the trigger
matching_facts: On July 19, 2024, a global IT outage was triggered by a faulty update from CrowdStrike, a leading cybersecurity firm.
